Repo: r:/APEX_NEW_VERSION/slicer_ux (Apex, a 3D-printer slicer UI: React/TS + Babylon.js viewport + shadcn panels, event-bus architecture via `window.dispatchEvent`/`addEventListener` with `apex-*` CustomEvents, no shared state/store). Read CLAUDE.md at repo root first for full architecture conventions before planning.

## Goal
Design an implementation plan for a "color by" selector added to the G-code Preview space's legend panel (see attached screenshot description: a "Type de ligne" legend table with swatch/duration/percentage/length/weight columns and a visibility checkbox per row — currently colors the 3D toolpath by line-type category only). The user wants a selector letting them recolor the 3D toolpath preview by one of ~15 criteria instead, ONE MODE ACTIVE AT A TIME (no cumulative overlay). This plan phase is implementation design only — no code should be written yet; another turn will implement it after the user reviews this plan.

## Confirmed requirements from user Q&A (must ground the plan in these, do not re-litigate)
- Single active color-by mode at a time; switching mode fully recolors the toolpath and replaces the legend table's content/columns for that mode.
- Criteria to support (some now, some to leave as clear extension points — final plan should propose which ship in v1 vs. which are stubbed/deferred, with rationale):
  1. Type de ligne (existing, must remain default/first)
  2. Vitesse (feed rate, mot F)
  3. Température (buse ; plateau si elle varie) — NOTE: gcodeLayer.ts parser currently does NOT parse M104/M109/M140/M190 at all — this requires new parsing.
  4. Hauteur de couche — NOTE: not currently computed; would come from per-move Z delta between layer changes, or generator-specific comments (none currently parsed).
  5. Vitesse du ventilateur — NOTE: M106/M107 not currently parsed at all.
  6. Largeur de ligne — user decided: use generator comment if present (e.g. Orca/Bambu/Prusa `;WIDTH:`), else ESTIMATE via width = E_volume / (distance × layer_height). Confirmed acceptable to compute even though width is normally a fixed slicer-profile setting, since this app only reads raw .gcode with no profile access.
  7. Débit volumétrique (mm³/s)
  8. Temps écoulé (temps machine cumulé depuis le début)
  9. Accélération (M204/M205 already partially tracked in parser as modal accel/jerk locals, but discarded per-move — see below)
  10. Vitesse angulaire de l'axe C (Apex-specific polar kinematics: rotation speed of the bed)
  11. Inclinaison de la tête / axe B (Apex-specific: B angle in degrees, already stored per-move as `GCodeMove.b`)
  12. Rapport vitesse / vitesse max de la couche (relative speed within current layer, 0-100%)
  13. Score de risque de défaut (heuristic combining high speed + overhang + low cooling) — user confirmed this must be plain TypeScript computed at parse/build time, NOT a separate Python/C++ process — app ships as an Electron .exe (browser-less framing was a red herring, still just a Chromium/Node runtime, so TS-only is correct and was confirmed by the user)
  14. Longueur du segment
  15. Pression d'extrusion relative (E per mm, distinct from volumetric flow — simpler ratio)
- Do NOT implement yet. This is a planning task; the user will greenlight implementation separately (another task is in progress concurrently, per user).

## Exact current-state facts already gathered (from a prior Explore pass) — use these, do not re-derive
- `src/components/gcodeLayer.ts` (~1477 lines): parser (`parseGCode`) + Babylon rendering layer (`createGCodeLayer`), all in one file.
  - `GCodeMove` interface (lines 41-51): only `{ x, y, z, b, extruding, type }` — no speed/temp/fan/width fields. Per-move feed rate, E-delta, deposits, accel/jerk are tracked in **parallel local arrays** (`feeds[]`, `eDeltas[]`, `deposits[]`, `accels[]`, `jerks[]`, `accelsToDecel[]`) inside `parseGCode()` but are **discarded** — not returned on `ParsedGCode`, only used to compute cumulative `times[]` and aggregate `lineStats` (per-LineTypeId totals: time/filamentMm/massG), then thrown away.
  - `ParsedGCode` interface (lines 63-92): `kind, moves, times (Float64Array cumulative), minZ/maxZ/maxR/minC/maxC, extrudingCount, lineStats (Record<LineTypeId, {time,filamentMm,massG}>), markers (retraction/unretraction/seam move-index arrays), generator, printer, nonPlanar, bedCenter, conversion, offPlate`. No numeric per-move arrays returned.
  - M-codes parsed today: ONLY M82, M83, M203, M204, M205, plus a Klipper `SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT` line. **M104/M109/M140/M190 (temperature) and M106/M107 (fan) are entirely unparsed** — must be added.
  - F-word / feed: `feed` modal var, updated on G0/G1/G2/G3 when `w.F` present; `feeds.push(feed)` on every `push()` call — so per-move *commanded* feed is trivially available at parse time (mm/min). For cartesian moves, ACTUAL kinematically-limited speed (post trapezoid/junction planning) is computed inside `planCartesianTimes()` (lines 186-253) as `vp`/junction speeds but not returned — only cumulative `times[]` escapes. Approx per-move actual speed can be derived as `chordLength/(times[k]-times[k-1])` by the caller without modifying the planner, OR the planner can be extended to also emit a `speeds: Float64Array` parallel to `times`.
  - Polar (Apex) vs cartesian detection: one-shot `polar` flag set true the first time a G0/G1 line has a B-word (line 452); never resets. `kind = polar ? 'polar' : 'cartesian'`.
  - Arc (G2/G3) subdivision happens in `parseGCode` itself (lines 462-503), emitting many `moves[]` entries via `push()` — so any per-move numeric field added to `GCodeMove`/parallel array will automatically be correctly subdivided across arc segments IF set consistently inside `push()`.
  - `lineStats` accumulation (lines 599-606): simple loop bucketing `times[k]-times[k-1]` and `deposits[k]` by `moves[k].type` into `emptyStats()` (Record<LineTypeId, LineTypeStat>). This is the ONLY existing aggregation pattern; there is no histogram/min-max range aggregation pattern for continuous values anywhere — would need new aggregation code for numeric legends (e.g. per-file min/max of speed/temp/etc., needed to build a gradient legend scale).
  - Markers (retraction/unretraction/seam): stored as sorted `Uint32Array` move-indices in `ParsedGCode.markers`, keyed by `MarkerTypeId = Extract<LineTypeId,'retraction'|'unretraction'|'seam'>`.
  - Babylon rendering: `buildBeadMesh()` (lines 841-947) builds ONE mesh per discrete extrusion `LineTypeId`, taking a SINGLE `material: BABYLON.Material` param, assigned via `mesh.material = material` (flat per-mesh color, no vertex colors, no `VertexData.colors` anywhere). `buildPathMesh()` (951-1002) similarly builds a `BABYLON.LinesMesh` with `mesh.color = color` (one flat Color3 per mesh) for travel/wipe. `buildMarkerMesh()` (1005-1030) is one shared material per marker type across thin instances.
  - Material construction (lines 1226-1239): one `StandardMaterial` per extrusion LineTypeId built ONCE at layer-creation time from `LINE_TYPES` colors (`BABYLON.Color3.FromHexString`).
  - `load()` (lines 1406-1447): for each LineTypeId with `kind==='extrusion'`, builds one mesh via `include = (k) => moves[k].type === t.id` predicate; for travel/wipe similarly; for markers, one mesh per marker type. Visibility toggle (`setLineTypeVisibility`, ~1453-1456) just flips `mesh.setEnabled(bool)` — no rebuild.
  - Live/in-progress trailing segment (`liveBead`/`liveLine`, `updateLive()`, lines ~1346-1388) also picks color from the same per-type material/color maps — must be updated in parallel for any new color mode so the live head trail matches.
  - **No gradient/colormap/lerp utility exists anywhere in the repo** (`BABYLON.Color3.Lerp` unused repo-wide, confirmed via grep). A numeric→color gradient helper must be built from scratch.
  - **Structural implication**: today's "one mesh per discrete category, flat material" design does not extend to continuous gradients without either (a) per-vertex vertex-colors on a single big mesh per color-mode (requires new VertexData.colors plumbing + a vertex-color-aware material, e.g. StandardMaterial with `.disableLighting`+ emissive-only or Babylon's vertex-color pipeline), or (b) bucketing continuous values into N discrete color bands (reuse existing one-mesh-per-bucket approach, less smooth but structurally simpler/lower risk). The plan MUST pick and justify one of these two rendering strategies (or a hybrid: discrete categories keep current per-mesh-material approach; continuous numeric modes use per-vertex color on a merged mesh).
  - No `;WIDTH`, `;LAYER_HEIGHT`, or other per-line/per-layer slicer metadata comments are parsed anywhere today (only `;TYPE:`/`;FEATURE:` and a generic header `key:value` parser for file-level header fields). Any width/layer-height mode needs new comment regexes added to `handleComment()`.
- `src/components/gcodeLineTypes.ts`: `LINE_TYPES: LineTypeInfo[]` (16 entries: id/label/description/color/kind/visibleByDefault), `LineTypeVisibility = Record<LineTypeId,boolean>`, `DEFAULT_LINE_VISIBILITY`, `LINE_TYPE_BY_ID`, `resolveLineType()` alias matcher.
- `src/hooks/use-gcode-preview.ts` (~406 lines): owns `GCodeFileInfo` (name/kind/lineStats/totalTime/generator/printer/nonPlanar/conversion/moves/extruding/minZ/maxZ/minC/maxC — no numeric-mode ranges yet), `lineVisibility` state + `setLineVisible`, dispatches `apex-gcode-line-visibility` CustomEvent on change (mirrors the general event-bus pattern from CLAUDE.md). This hook is the natural place to add new `colorBy` mode state + a new `apex-gcode-color-by` CustomEvent dispatch (following the exact existing pattern for `apex-gcode-line-visibility`), plus extending `GCodeFileInfo` with per-file numeric ranges (min/max) needed for gradient legends.
- `src/components/GCodeLineTypeLegend.tsx` + `.module.scss`: memoized grid-table component (header row + per-LINE_TYPES-entry rows: swatch/name/duration/%/length/weight/checkbox), mounted in `src/pages/Index.tsx` (lines ~255-293) as `<CategoriesSidebar previewUpperContent={<GCodeLineTypeLegend .../>} previewLowerHeader={<GCodeInfoPanel/>} previewBelowContent={<GCodeConversionCard/>} previewLowerContent={<GCodeSpeedSelector/>} />`. `CategoriesSidebar.tsx` itself is a pure layout shell with 4 slot props, no direct knowledge of G-code components.
- `src/components/GCodeSpeedSelector.tsx` + `.module.scss`: reference pattern for a small control in this panel — a custom log-scale slider PLUS a `role="radiogroup"` segmented-button group bound to fixed presets (`GCODE_SPEED_OPTIONS`), with a staggered fade-up entrance animation (`containerVariants`/`itemVariants`, same cascade reused in the legend). Does NOT dispatch a CustomEvent (plain controlled props, since it doesn't need to reach the Babylon layer directly) — unlike line-visibility which does need the event-bus round-trip since Babylon lives outside React. A "color by" selector, since it MUST reach `gcodeLayer.ts`'s Babylon code, needs the CustomEvent pattern like `apex-gcode-line-visibility`, not the plain-prop pattern like speed.
- `src/components/gcodeGenerator.ts`: only detects which slicer produced the file (header signature regexes + line-type-naming-style heuristic); no per-line metadata parsing.
- CLAUDE.md conventions to respect: event-bus (`apex-*` CustomEvents) for Viewport3D/Babylon-layer ↔ React panel communication (grep `apex-` before adding new events — reuse if an existing one already carries the needed data, but none does here); `*.module.scss` pairing per component for bespoke visual treatment; shadcn/ui + Tailwind for standard layout; don't edit `src/components/ui/*` directly; new components go in `src/components/`; after adding to the tree it must be rendered in `Index.tsx` or it's invisible; toast via `src/utils/toast.ts`. User's standing preference (from memory, non-negotiable): **fluidity above all — zero visible stutter in preview/animations (tolerance ≤ 0.1mm)** — this must shape the plan's performance approach (e.g. mesh rebuild cost when switching color-by mode or reloading a large file, avoiding per-frame allocation in the live-trail update, gradient computation cost).

## What the plan must cover
1. **Data model extension** — exactly which new fields need to be parsed/tracked in `gcodeLayer.ts`'s `parseGCode()` and threaded onto `GCodeMove`/`ParsedGCode` for each v1 criterion (propose which of the 15 ship in v1 given real parsing cost vs. which are natural "phase 2" stubs — e.g. temperature/fan need entirely new M-code parsing, "score de risque" needs several other fields to already exist so it should ship last within v1 or be phase 2). Be concrete: name the new M-code cases, new comment regexes, new parallel arrays or GCodeMove fields, and how per-move numeric values survive arc subdivision (`push()`).
2. **Rendering strategy** — decisively pick discrete-bucket-materials vs. per-vertex-gradient (or a hybrid keyed by whether the mode is categorical vs. continuous), and describe the concrete Babylon changes needed (VertexData.colors plumbing if per-vertex, or bucket-count/threshold design if discrete-bucketed), covering both `buildBeadMesh`/`buildPathMesh` and the live trailing segment update path, and how mode-switching triggers a rebuild (vs. today's cheap `setEnabled` visibility toggle) without violating the fluidity requirement — e.g. rebuild only the changed mode's meshes, reuse geometry across mode switches where color is the only thing changing, avoid rebuilding on every frame.
3. **Colormap utility** — a new small module (e.g. `src/components/gcodeColormap.ts`) for numeric→Color3 mapping (propose a specific perceptually-reasonable colormap approach, e.g. a 2 or 3-stop or viridis-like HSV lerp), reusable across all continuous modes, with per-file min/max normalization sourced from new `ParsedGCode`/`GCodeFileInfo` range fields.
4. **Event/state wiring** — new `apex-gcode-color-by` CustomEvent (or best-fitting name after grepping existing `apex-*` names) dispatched from `use-gcode-preview.ts` mirroring `apex-gcode-line-visibility`'s exact existing pattern; new `colorBy` state + setter in the hook; extending `GCodeFileInfo` with the numeric ranges/legend data needed per mode.
5. **UI** — where exactly the selector control goes (propose reusing `previewUpperContent` above/inside the legend vs. a new slot), what widget shape fits ~15 options grouped sensibly (the user separately confirmed too many for a flat single-row segmented control — propose e.g. a dropdown/popover with grouped sections, following existing shadcn/ui + Tailwind + this repo's glassmorphism `.module.scss` visual language, reusing `GCodeSpeedSelector`'s segmented-button/checkbox visual patterns where they fit), and how `GCodeLineTypeLegend`'s table body/columns change per mode (discrete rows w/ checkboxes for categorical modes like today, vs. a gradient scale + min/max/avg readout for continuous modes) — name the concrete component/prop changes.
6. **Extension points** — how a future criterion (16th+) is added with minimal ceremony, given the chosen architecture.
7. **Verification plan** — how to manually test end-to-end (`pnpm dev`, load a real polar Apex .gcode and a real cartesian slicer .gcode with temp/fan/width comments if available, switch through each mode, confirm legend updates, confirm live playback trail recolors, confirm mode switch has no visible stutter per the fluidity requirement, confirm visibility toggling still works for categorical modes).

Do not write any code. Produce a structured implementation plan (phases, concrete files touched, key function signatures/interfaces to add or change, and the rendering-strategy decision with justification) suitable for a human to review before implementation begins. Where you must make a judgment call the user hasn't specified, state your recommendation and rationale clearly so it can be flagged back to the user if needed.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project overview

Apex is a 3D printer slicer UI developed by Aelox Hardware: a Babylon.js viewport (build plate, printer boundary shader, model loading/manipulation) surrounded by shadcn/ui panels for file management, printer/filament config, texture editing, and slicing. This repo was originally scaffolded from the `vite_react_shadcn_ts` template — expect those scaffolding conventions (see AI_RULES.md) alongside hand-written slicer-specific code.

## Commands

```bash
pnpm install       # this repo uses pnpm (pnpm-lock.yaml / pnpm-workspace.yaml present)
pnpm dev           # vite dev server on port 8080
pnpm build         # production build
pnpm build:dev     # development-mode build
pnpm lint          # eslint .
pnpm preview       # preview the production build
```

There is no test runner configured in this repo (no test script, no test files).

## Architecture

### Global event bus, not shared state

There is no state management library and no shared React context between the sidebar/panel components and the 3D viewport. Instead, `Viewport3D.tsx` and every panel component communicate exclusively through `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(...))` / `window.addEventListener(...)`, using a fixed set of `apex-*` event names, e.g.:

- `apex-tool-changed` — Sidebar → Viewport3D (select/move/rotate/scale/delete tool switch)
- `apex-mesh-selected`, `apex-mesh-deleted` — Viewport3D → ModelStatusBox, SliceSidebar, SliceModal, TextureEditorModal
- `apex-model-hover` — Viewport3D → ModelHoverTooltip

   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation

   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`

   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>

  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).

    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)

    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.

    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.

    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. ## 1. Data model extension (`src/components/gcodeLayer.ts`)

### 1.1 New parallel arrays inside `parseGCode()`, alongside existing `feeds[]`/`eDeltas[]`/etc.

All arrays are indexed identically to `moves[]`/`times[]` (index 0 unused/zero, matching existing
convention), pushed once per call to `push()` so arc subdivision (`push()` called per subdivided
arc segment in the G2/G3 handler) automatically produces correct per-segment values — no separate
handling needed for arcs, exactly as `feeds`/`eDeltas`/`accels` already work today.

New modal state (top of `parseGCode`, alongside `feed`, `accelPrint`, etc.):
```
let nozzleTemp = 0;       // °C, from M104/M109 S
let bedTemp = 0;          // °C, from M140/M190 S
let fanSpeed = 0;         // 0-100 %, from M106 S (0-255 scaled) / M107 (=0)
```

New M-code cases in the `if (cmd[1] === 'M')` block:
```
else if (num === 104 || num === 109) { if (w.S >= 0) nozzleTemp = w.S; }
else if (num === 140 || num === 190) { if (w.S >= 0) bedTemp = w.S; }
else if (num === 106) { if (w.S >= 0) fanSpeed = Math.round((w.S / 255) * 100); }
else if (num === 107) { fanSpeed = 0; }
```
(M109/M190 are "wait" variants; for a static-preview colorizer we only care about the commanded
setpoint, not the wait — so treating them identically to M104/M140 is correct and simpler than
tracking "reached" state.)

New parallel arrays populated inside `push()` (mirroring `feeds.push(feed)`):
```

bedTemps.push(bedTemp);
fans.push(fanSpeed);
```

`feeds[]` already holds the commanded F (mm/min) per move — sufficient for "Vitesse" in v1 as a

correct for the vast majority of moves which do reach cruise speed) and note actual-speed as a
phase-2 refinement — flag this trade-off to the user.

### 1.3 Layer height (#4) and line width (#6)

New bookkeeping in `parseGCode`, cartesian path only (polar has no discrete "layers" in the same
sense — treat layer-height/width as "n/a" for polar in v1, another judgment call to flag):
- Track `layerStartZ` / `prevLayerZ`: on each extruding move, if `mv.z` differs from the last
  extruding Z seen by more than `1e-4`, that's a layer change; `layerHeight = mv.z - prevLayerZ`.

- New comment regex `WIDTH_RE = /^\s*WIDTH\s*[:=]\s*([\d.]+)/i` parsed in `handleComment`, alongside

  to `NaN` if not re-stated (some slicers emit per-line `;WIDTH:` comments before each new width

- Fallback estimate when `explicitWidth` is `NaN`: `width = eVolumeMm3 / (segmentLengthMm * layerHeightMm)`,

  negligible next to mesh rebuild cost.)

Needs a per-layer max-speed lookup. Two-pass: first pass (right after `times[]`/`feeds[]` exist)
builds `layerMaxFeed: Map<number /* layer index */, number>` keyed by the same layer-change

```ts
  ...
  // Nouveaux champs numériques par mouvement (Float32Array, un par critère de coloration continu) :
  feedMmS: Float32Array;      // vitesse commandée F, mm/s
```

## 3. Rendering strategy - decision

Hybrid, keyed by categorical vs. continuous, as the requirements doc's own analysis suggests:

- Categorical mode (#1, "Type de ligne"): keep the existing architecture completely unchanged -
  one mesh per LineTypeId, one flat StandardMaterial, setEnabled for visibility. Zero risk, zero
  regression surface, since this is the default/first mode and must remain exactly as-is per
  requirements.

- Continuous modes (all others in v1): switch to per-vertex vertex colors on ONE merged bead mesh
  + ONE merged travel/wipe line mesh, replacing the per-LineTypeId mesh split for the duration that
  a continuous mode is active. Justification:
  - Bucketing into N discrete bands (the alternative) would still require picking a band count,
    causes visible banding contrary to the "fluidity"/visual-quality bar for a gradient legend, and
    doesn't actually save implementation complexity here - buildBeadMesh/buildPathMesh already
    build one mesh per include() predicate, so a bucketed version needs the same amount of new code
    as a vertex-color version but produces a visibly worse result.
  - Per-vertex color avoids the "one mesh per category" ceiling (13 modes x potentially many
    buckets each would multiply draw calls); a single merged mesh per continuous mode is actually a
    net draw-call reduction vs. today's ~11 extrusion-type meshes, which helps fluidity, not hurts it.
  - Concrete Babylon changes: extend buildBeadMesh/buildPathMesh with an optional
    vertexColor: (k: number) => BABYLON.Color3 callback (mutually exclusive with the existing
    material/color param - when provided, write VertexData.colors (Float32Array, 4 floats/vertex,
    alpha 1) computed once per vertex written in the existing ring/position-writing loop, no extra
    pass). Material becomes a single shared "vertex-color aware" StandardMaterial: recommend
    mat.disableLighting = true; mat.emissiveColor = Color3.White() so vertex colors multiply
    emissive directly, avoiding any lighting-interaction surprises (verify mat.diffuseColor stays
    white if disableLighting is left false instead, so it doesn't tint the vertex colors); keep
    backFaceCulling = false as today.
  - buildPathMesh (LinesMesh) needs per-vertex color support too - Babylon's LinesMesh supports
    per-vertex colors natively via VertexData.colors plus mesh.useVertexColor = true - set that
    flag and write colors alongside positions in the existing vertex-writing loop.

- Mode switching / rebuild cost: switching colorBy requires a geometry rebuild only when crossing
  the categorical<->continuous boundary or between two different continuous modes (new vertex
  colors need different values). To respect the fluidity requirement (<=0.1mm/zero stutter):
  - Rebuild happens once, synchronously, on mode change - NOT per frame. This matches today's
    load() cost model (already a full rebuild on file load); a mode switch is strictly cheaper (no
    re-parsing, geometry/topology identical, only the color buffer changes).
  - Key optimization: cache the merged-mesh positions/normals/indices per kind (extrusion merged
    bead geometry, travel+wipe merged line geometry) built once at load() time regardless of
    initial mode, and on a continuous-mode switch only recompute+upload the VertexData.colors
    buffer via mesh.updateVerticesData(BABYLON.VertexBuffer.ColorKind, ...) - no
    VertexData.applyToMesh (positions/indices unchanged), avoiding the expensive parts of a full
    rebuild. This is the single most important perf decision for the "no stutter" requirement.
  - Only the very first switch away from categorical (or into it) needs a topology change (merging
    N per-type meshes into 1, or vice versa); cache BOTH geometry layouts (per-type AND merged)
    built once at load(), so subsequent toggling between categorical and any continuous mode is
    also just a setEnabled/color-buffer swap, never a rebuild. Given typical file sizes this
    roughly doubles peak geometry memory for the extrusion mesh set - acceptable trade for
    zero-stutter switching; flag this memory/latency trade-off to the user if very large files are
    a concern.

- Live trailing segment (updateLive, liveBead/liveLine): currently picks
  beadMaterials.get(m.type) / colors[type]. Extend to: in continuous mode, compute
  colorForMode(mode, next, parsed, tmpColor) once per frame (cheap, O(1), no allocation if
  tmpColor is a hoisted reusable BABYLON.Color3) and set liveBead.material.emissiveColor = tmpColor
  directly (since the live bead is a single small mesh, not vertex-colored, a flat material color
  update is fine and cheapest). Recommendation: flat live-color per frame - the live segment is
  tiny (<=1 move worth of geometry) so any visible mismatch with a gradient is imperceptible, and
  this avoids an updateVerticesData call every frame (better for fluidity than vertex-coloring the
  live strip too).

    export function colorForMode(mode: ColorByMode, k: number, parsed: ParsedGCode, out: BABYLON.Color3): BABYLON.Color3;

Recommendation: a 4-stop piecewise-linear RGB lerp (dark blue -> cyan -> yellow -> red), i.e. a
simplified viridis/turbo-style ramp, computed with plain arithmetic (no HSV conversion needed,
avoids hue-wraparound bugs, cheap enough for per-vertex use at parse/build time). Reuse
BABYLON.Color3.Lerp (confirmed unused today but perfectly fit for this) between the two bracketing
stops of t. This one function serves every continuous mode (#2,#3,#4,#5,#6,#7,#8,#9,#12,#14,#15) -
categorical mode (#1) keeps using LINE_TYPES[].color unchanged, never routed through this module.

## 3. Rendering strategy - decision

Hybrid, keyed by categorical vs. continuous, as the requirements doc's own analysis suggests:

- Categorical mode (#1, "Type de ligne"): keep the existing architecture completely unchanged -
  one mesh per LineTypeId, one flat StandardMaterial, setEnabled for visibility. Zero risk, zero
  regression surface, since this is the default/first mode and must remain exactly as-is per
  requirements.

- Continuous modes (all others in v1): switch to per-vertex vertex colors on ONE merged bead mesh
  + ONE merged travel/wipe line mesh, replacing the per-LineTypeId mesh split for the duration that
  a continuous mode is active. Justification:
  - Bucketing into N discrete bands (the alternative) would still require picking a band count,
    causes visible banding contrary to the "fluidity"/visual-quality bar for a gradient legend, and
    doesn't actually save implementation complexity here - buildBeadMesh/buildPathMesh already
    build one mesh per include() predicate, so a bucketed version needs the same amount of new code
    as a vertex-color version but produces a visibly worse result.
  - Per-vertex color avoids the "one mesh per category" ceiling (13 modes x potentially many
    buckets each would multiply draw calls); a single merged mesh per continuous mode is actually a
    net draw-call reduction vs. today's ~11 extrusion-type meshes, which helps fluidity, not hurts it.
  - Concrete Babylon changes: extend buildBeadMesh/buildPathMesh with an optional
    vertexColor: (k: number) => BABYLON.Color3 callback (mutually exclusive with the existing
    material/color param - when provided, write VertexData.colors (Float32Array, 4 floats/vertex,
    alpha 1) computed once per vertex written in the existing ring/position-writing loop, no extra
    pass). Material becomes a single shared "vertex-color aware" StandardMaterial: recommend
    mat.disableLighting = true; mat.emissiveColor = Color3.White() so vertex colors multiply
    emissive directly, avoiding any lighting-interaction surprises (verify mat.diffuseColor stays
    white if disableLighting is left false instead, so it doesn't tint the vertex colors); keep
    backFaceCulling = false as today.
  - buildPathMesh (LinesMesh) needs per-vertex color support too - Babylon's LinesMesh supports
    per-vertex colors natively via VertexData.colors plus mesh.useVertexColor = true - set that
    flag and write colors alongside positions in the existing vertex-writing loop.

- Mode switching / rebuild cost: switching colorBy requires a geometry rebuild only when crossing
  the categorical<->continuous boundary or between two different continuous modes (new vertex
  colors need different values). To respect the fluidity requirement (<=0.1mm/zero stutter):
  - Rebuild happens once, synchronously, on mode change - NOT per frame. This matches today's
    load() cost model (already a full rebuild on file load); a mode switch is strictly cheaper (no
    re-parsing, geometry/topology identical, only the color buffer changes).
  - Key optimization: cache the merged-mesh positions/normals/indices per kind (extrusion merged
    bead geometry, travel+wipe merged line geometry) built once at load() time regardless of
    initial mode, and on a continuous-mode switch only recompute+upload the VertexData.colors
    buffer via mesh.updateVerticesData(BABYLON.VertexBuffer.ColorKind, ...) - no
    VertexData.applyToMesh (positions/indices unchanged), avoiding the expensive parts of a full
    rebuild. This is the single most important perf decision for the "no stutter" requirement.
  - Only the very first switch away from categorical (or into it) needs a topology change (merging
    N per-type meshes into 1, or vice versa); cache BOTH geometry layouts (per-type AND merged)
    built once at load(), so subsequent toggling between categorical and any continuous mode is
    also just a setEnabled/color-buffer swap, never a rebuild. Given typical file sizes this
    roughly doubles peak geometry memory for the extrusion mesh set - acceptable trade for
    zero-stutter switching; flag this memory/latency trade-off to the user if very large files are
    a concern.

- Live trailing segment (updateLive, liveBead/liveLine): currently picks
  beadMaterials.get(m.type) / colors[type]. Extend to: in continuous mode, compute
  colorForMode(mode, next, parsed, tmpColor) once per frame (cheap, O(1), no allocation if
  tmpColor is a hoisted reusable BABYLON.Color3) and set liveBead.material.emissiveColor = tmpColor
  directly (since the live bead is a single small mesh, not vertex-colored, a flat material color
  update is fine and cheapest). Recommendation: flat live-color per frame - the live segment is
  tiny (<=1 move worth of geometry) so any visible mismatch with a gradient is imperceptible, and
  this avoids an updateVerticesData call every frame (better for fluidity than vertex-coloring the
  live strip too).

## 4. Event/state wiring

New CustomEvent, following apex-gcode-line-visibility's exact pattern (grepped - no existing
apex-* event carries a color-mode payload):

    // use-gcode-preview.ts
    export type ColorByMode = 'lineType' | 'speed' | 'accel' | 'headAngle' | 'segmentLength'
      | 'elapsedTime' | 'extrusionRatio' | 'volumetricFlow' | 'layerSpeedRatio'
      | 'lineWidth' | 'layerHeight' | 'temperature' | 'fanSpeed'; // v1 set per section 0

    const [colorBy, setColorByState] = useState<ColorByMode>('lineType');
    useEffect(() => {
      window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apex-gcode-color-by', { detail: { mode: colorBy } }));
    }, [colorBy]);
    const setColorBy = useCallback((mode: ColorByMode) => setColorByState(mode), []);

Viewport3D.tsx adds onGCodeColorBy mirroring onGCodeLineVisibility (add/remove listener next to
the existing ones, call a new gcodeLayer.setColorBy(mode) method on the GCodeLayer interface).

GCodeFileInfo (in use-gcode-preview.ts) gains the per-mode range data needed for legend display:

    colorByRanges: ColorByRanges; // from ParsedGCode.ranges, section 1.7

threaded through in loadText()'s setFileInfo({...}) call alongside the existing fields.

## 5. UI

Selector placement: reuse previewUpperContent - put the mode selector as a new small header
control directly above GCodeLineTypeLegend's existing header row. Recommendation: extend
GCodeLineTypeLegend in place (rather than splitting into a separate wrapper component) - it
already owns the legend table; adding the mode dropdown as its own header row above the grid keeps
the "swap legend content per mode" logic co-located with the legend body it swaps, per requirement
#5's own framing ("how GCodeLineTypeLegend's table body/columns change per mode").

Widget shape for 13 (v1) options: per the user's confirmed constraint (too many for a flat
segmented control), use a shadcn Popover + grouped list (Radix primitives already installed per
AI_RULES.md), trigger button styled like existing glassmorphism controls
(GCodeLineTypeLegend.module.scss / GCodeSpeedSelector.module.scss visual language - reuse the
checkboxRow/segment button treatment for the trigger's rest state). Group sections inside the
popover:
- "Type de ligne" (single item, always first, default)
- "Cinematique" - Vitesse, Acceleration, Inclinaison tete (B), Longueur segment, Temps ecoule
- "Extrusion" - Debit volumetrique, Pression E relative, Largeur de ligne, Hauteur de couche
- "Vitesse relative" - Rapport vitesse/vitesse max de couche
- "Thermique / refroidissement" - Temperature, Vitesse ventilateur
(Angular C speed / risk score omitted from v1 menu per section 0, added as a disabled/greyed
"Bientot disponible" group only if the user wants visible signposting - otherwise fully absent
until phase 2.)

Each popover row: label + tiny icon/swatch preview (for continuous modes, a small gradient bar
snippet using the same viridisLike ramp, for visual consistency with the eventual full legend
gradient bar).

Legend body change per mode:
- Categorical (lineType): unchanged - current grid/rows/checkboxes exactly as today.
- Continuous mode: replace the per-row grid with:
  - A single horizontal gradient bar (CSS linear-gradient, stops sampled from viridisLike at 5-6
    points, computed once per mode - hardcode the same stop colors as literal hex in the
    .module.scss/inline style so the CSS bar and the Babylon coloring are visually identical).
  - Min / Avg / Max readout row beneath it, sourced from fileInfo.colorByRanges[mode] (section
    1.7), formatted with the mode's unit (mm/s, degC, %, mm, s, mm3/s) - a new small
    formatColorByValue(mode, value) helper co-located in GCodeLineTypeLegend.tsx.
  - No per-row visibility checkboxes in continuous mode (there's no discrete category to toggle) -
    but the existing categorical visibility state (lineVisibility) must remain independently
    respected by the 3D layer regardless of colorBy (a continuous color mode still only shows
    line-types the user has toggled on) - confirm this stays orthogonal: setLineTypeVisibility and
    setColorBy are separate GCodeLayer methods, so visibility filtering (include() predicates) and
    coloring are already architecturally decoupled by this plan (section 3), good.

## 6. Extension points (16th+ criterion)

Given the chosen architecture, adding a new continuous criterion requires only:
1. A new parallel array (or derived-on-the-fly computation) added to ParsedGCode in gcodeLayer.ts.
2. One new entry in the ColorByMode union + one case in colorForMode() in gcodeColormap.ts.
3. One new popover row (with its group) in the selector.
4. One new unit/label mapping in formatColorByValue.
No changes to buildBeadMesh/buildPathMesh/updateLive/the event wiring are needed - they're already
generic over "a function that returns a color for move k." Adding a new categorical criterion
(rather than continuous) is more work (needs its own discrete-bucket mesh-per-value scheme like
LineTypeId today) - flag this asymmetry to the user; all 13 v1 criteria except #1 are continuous
by design, which is why the hybrid strategy optimizes for that case.

## 7. Verification plan

1. pnpm dev, open the Preview space.
2. Load a real polar Apex .gcode (B-word moves) - confirm: default "Type de ligne" mode renders
   identically to before (no regression); switching to "Vitesse"/"Acceleration"/"Inclinaison tete"
   recolors the toolpath with a visible gradient; angular-C-speed and risk-score are absent from
   the menu (phase 2); temperature/fan show "n/a" or flat color if the polar file has no
   M104/M106 lines (verify graceful fallback, not a crash, when a mode's data is all-zero/no
   variation).
3. Load a real cartesian slicer .gcode that includes temperature/fan/;WIDTH: comments (e.g. an
   Orca/Bambu export) - confirm temperature and fan modes show real variation (if the file
   actually changes temps/fan mid-print; many single-temperature prints won't show a gradient -
   verify the min=max case renders a solid single color, not divide-by-zero/NaN).
4. For each of the 13 v1 modes: confirm legend swaps from table-with-checkboxes to
   gradient-bar-with-min/avg/max, values look plausible (e.g. speed in mm/s roughly matches known
   print speeds; layer height matches the file's known layer height).
5. Confirm visibility checkboxes still work correctly in categorical mode (toggle a line type off,
   confirm it disappears) and that switching to a continuous mode and back to categorical restores
   the exact same visibility state (no accidental reset).
6. Confirm live playback trail recolors correctly while a continuous mode is active and during
   playback (press play, watch the trailing bead segment match the color of the static prefix it
   extends).
7. Switch rapidly between all modes with a large file loaded (many thousands of moves) and confirm
   no visible stutter/frame hitch (per the <=0.1mm fluidity requirement) - this specifically tests
   the "cache both geometry layouts, only swap color buffer" optimization in section 3; if a hitch
   IS visible, that is the first place to profile (likely updateVerticesData size or an accidental
   full VertexData.applyToMesh being triggered instead of the targeted buffer update).
8. Confirm mode selection behaves predictably across loading a new file in the same session -
   recommend resetting colorBy to 'lineType' on new file load, consistent with the existing
   setConversion(IDLE_CONVERSION) reset already done in loadText().

## Open judgment calls to flag to the user before implementation

- Whether temperature (#3) and fan (#5) really belong in v1 given they need net-new M-code parsing
  (vs. everything else in v1 which reuses already-tracked modal state).
- Commanded-F speed vs. actual trapezoid-limited speed for "Vitesse" mode (recommend commanded F
  for v1 simplicity).
- Layer height / width / relative-layer-speed as "n/a" for polar files (no discrete layer concept
  in the same sense) - confirm acceptable.
- Angular C speed and risk score fully deferred to phase 2, not even shown as disabled stub in the
  v1 menu - confirm acceptable, or user may prefer a visible "Bientot disponible" placeholder.
- Doubling peak geometry memory (caching both per-type and merged mesh layouts) to guarantee
  zero-rebuild mode switching - confirm acceptable given "fluidity above all" preference, especially
  for very large G-code files.

3. **Rendering strategy (decided)**: hybrid — categorical "Type de ligne" keeps today's per-type-mesh/flat-material approach untouched; all continuous modes switch to per-vertex `VertexData.colors` on merged meshes. Key fluidity-preserving optimization: cache both per-type and merged geometry layouts once at `load()`, so mode switching only calls `updateVerticesData(ColorKind, ...)` — never a full geometry rebuild.

4. **New `gcodeColormap.ts`** with a 4-stop RGB lerp (reusing `BABYLON.Color3.Lerp`, confirmed unused today).

5. **Event/state wiring**: new `apex-gcode-color-by` event mirroring `apex-gcode-line-visibility` exactly.

7. **Extension points and a concrete verification plan** covering both real polar and cartesian files, stutter-testing, and visibility/mode-switch interaction.
